chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man is overcome by urine and cannot hold it back.' He (peace be upon him) said to me, 'When he cannot hold it back, then Allah is more deserving of excuse; he may make it [fall] into a bag.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who cannot control their urine?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the practical jurisprudence of *istibra’* (ensuring the bladder is empty) for those with incontinence (*mudha’*), ruling that Allah grants excuse for involuntary discharge. The directive to use a *khariata* (a cloth or bag) highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining ritual purity (*taharah*) through manageable physical means rather than strict abstinence, reflecting the principle of *al-mashaqqah tajlib al-taysir* (hardship brings ease).

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Mansour Bin Hazim who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man is desperate for the urination and he is not able upon withholding it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘When he is not able upon withholding it, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Closest with the Excusing. He can make it to be in a bag’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who has the urge to urinate and cannot hold it any longer. He (the Imam) said to me, ‘If he is not able to hold, Allah is the foremost to accept apologies, he can allow it to come out in a bag.”
